n: John sees another great sign: seven angels holding the seven last plagues, which complete God’s judgment on unrepentant wickedness.
He sees a sea of glass mixed with fire, and on it stand those who conquered the beast, its image, and its mark, holding harps from God.
Like Israel singing beside the Red Sea after escaping Egypt, they sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb: God’s works are great and His ways just and true.

f.g: Many manuscripts read ‘King of the nations.’

n: Who will not revere and glorify God? Only He is holy, and all nations will come and worship Him because His righteous judgments have been revealed.
Then John sees the heavenly temple—the tabernacle of the testimony—opened.

f.g: The tent housing the ark and the tablets of the covenant.

n: The seven angels come out wearing pure white linen and golden sashes, dressed like priests. Their judgments are a holy act.
One of the four living creatures hands them seven golden bowls filled with the wrath of the eternal God.

f.g: Wide, shallow bowls used in temple service.

n: The temple fills with smoke from God’s glory and power, and no one can enter until the seven plagues are finished—as when God’s glory filled Solomon’s temple.

f.w: filled with smoke from the glory of God
